# WO-2026-08-12-02 — Region granularity, the default-one quantity rule, and a scorer worth trusting

## Acceptance criteria

> **⛔ READ THIS FIRST — Warwick's calibration, which governs how your result will be read.**
> *"Do NOT treat the recalculated 61.5% as remotely close to done... **Do not come back celebrating
> another four percentage points.** The purpose of region granularity is to determine whether the
> architecture can move from 'roughly half right' into genuinely trustworthy territory... **Another
> result around 60–70% is NOT convergence. If smaller deterministic regions do not produce a large
> improvement, say so plainly and step out of the loop again** rather than starting another
> threshold/prompt round."*
> **A plainly-stated negative is the correct discharge of this order. Prompt tuning to move a number is not.**

**AC1 — the household default-one quantity rule, deterministic.** Warwick's ruling, and his examples ARE
the specification:
- *"Richmond 16 sausages"* → **1** pack of the 16-count product
- *"Ariel Pods 33"* → **1** pack of the 33-count product
- *"Cravendale milk x4"* → **4** bottles
- *"Cravendale milk"* → **1** bottle

**"Product-pack numbers are PRODUCT IDENTITY, not purchase quantity."** Quantity comes ONLY from explicit
evidence on the list, or this authorised household rule. **Terra must never infer quantity from a number
embedded in a product name.** Implement as a deterministic application-side rule — not a prompt request —
and unit-test each of the four cases above by name.

**AC2 — the scorer stops marking correct behaviour wrong.** A `null` quantity is **NOT** an error where
the page carries no explicit quantity and default-one applies. This directly retires 6 of the 9
wrong-quantity verdicts from WP-B15-29, which penalised exactly the behaviour the order mandated.

**AC3 — the 39-line acceptance fixture. BUILD THIS BEFORE THE REGION CHANGE.** Warwick: *"the next
percentage is not decision-grade until the scorer is corrected."* From the known photograph, map each of
the 39 source lines to: **expected visible/source interpretation** · **intended catalogue/product identity
where established** · **explicit quantity where present, otherwise household-default 1**.
⛔ **"This is TEST DATA ONLY. Do not turn it into production logic."** No production path may read it.
**The discriminating case it must resolve:** `"2 chips with skins on"` → *ASDA Crispy Skin-On Fries*.
WP-B15-29's fuzzy join could not reconcile that despite it being the known correct mapping, and reported
it as an **invention** — which is how three of five reported inventions were measurement noise.

**AC4 — two separate score layers. Never one collapsed "correct %".**
**(A) PHOTO / SOURCE-TRUTH QUALITY** — 39 expected · lines detected · omissions · invented PHOTO lines ·
duplicates · visible-text/interpretation errors · explicit quantity errors · correctly surfaced UNKNOWNs.
**(B) IDENTITY RESOLUTION QUALITY**, per detected line — correct catalogue/household product · wrong
identity · unresolved/UNKNOWN.
*"That prevents an OCR/coverage failure from being confused with a catalogue-matching failure."*

**AC5 — smaller deterministic application-owned regions.** Move from 3 regions to **something like 6–8**
(`TARGET_STRIP_HEIGHT_PX = 700`, `MIN_STRIPS = 2`, `MAX_STRIPS = 6` and the 15% overlap are the current
constants). **Modest overlap is mandatory so a line near a boundary cannot silently vanish.** The regions
stay **application-owned and deterministic** — Terra never proposes its own coordinates.
**Prove coverage, do not assume it:** demonstrate that every one of the 39 known source lines falls inside
at least one region, and that no line sits only at a boundary. **⛔ Do NOT create 39 individual routine
calls** — Warwick: *"without creating an API-call farm."*

**AC6 — inspect regions individually, not bundled.** The real A/B has already shown individual region
inspection materially outperforms bundling on this exact photograph. Architecture stays simple:
*prepared image → deterministic region coverage → Terra region inspection with household context →
constrained candidate ID / UNKNOWN → deterministic reconciliation → provenance/sanity checks → final
source truth.*

**AC7 — deterministic reconciliation across overlapping regions.** Overlap means the same handwritten line
will legitimately appear in two regions. Reconcile deterministically: the same line seen twice is ONE line,
not a duplicate and not two. Two genuinely different lines are never merged. **This is where overlap either
pays for itself or creates a new duplicate class — measure which.**

**AC8 — the structural wins are REGRESSION-PROTECTED, not merely retained.** Warwick lists them and they
must not regress: closed candidate enum · `strict:true` · free brand invention impossible · UNKNOWN
remains valid · region-1 defect fixed · Richmond quantity class fixed · application-owned region grounding
· household context retained · confidence as inspection trigger and never truth authority. **Assert them in
tests**, so a regression fails a suite rather than being noticed in a percentage.

**AC9 — the measured re-test, reported in both layers**, with **calls, wall time and real gateway cost**.
Cost framing, quoted: *"$0.1375 is nowhere near an API-cost crisis. If better region coverage doubles or
even modestly exceeds that cost but produces a trustworthy weekly shop, that is economically sane...
Optimise once the product works. **Do not save pennies by accepting rubbish.**"*

**AC10 — the remaining real defects, pursued independently and reported.** In-enum variant confusion (three
Vanish variants where the page has one) · the wrong pasta flavour · duplicate resolution · **four-way
provenance persistence, still incomplete — the prototype writes no DB rows.** Report what finer regions
did to each; fix only what falls inside your surface.

**The bar, unchanged and quoted:** ~95%+ automatically correct on the 39-line source truth · ZERO invented
PHOTO lines · ZERO silent quantity guesses · ZERO household enrichment masquerading as PHOTO · no large
silent omission class · genuine ambiguity surfaced explicitly rather than guessed. *38 correct / 1 UNKNOWN
/ 0 inventions* is **excellent**; *35 correct / 4 UNKNOWN / 0 inventions* **may also be product-usable**.

- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/asdair/pipeline/agenticVisionPrototype` → exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass.

## Sequencing

**0. READ-BACK, then HOLD.** Restate the outcome, your plan, what this order failed to settle, and what
looks wrong — then stop and wait for Larry's acceptance before writing code. Your WP-B15-29 read-back
found four real defects in that order and was upheld in full; apply the same scrutiny here. One amended
order and one further read-back are available if you find a material defect.

**1. MEASUREMENT FIRST — AC1 → AC2 → AC3 → AC4.** This ordering is Warwick's explicit instruction and is
not negotiable: *"fix the measurement before trusting the next percentage."* Build the default-one rule,
correct the scorer, build the 39-line fixture, split the two score layers — **and re-score the EXISTING

like-for-like baseline and tells us immediately how much of WP-B15-29's result was measurement noise.

**2. THEN THE REGION CHANGE — AC5 → AC6 → AC7.** Prove coverage of all 39 lines before spending money on
a live run; a run over regions that do not cover the page answers nothing.

**3. AC8** — pin the structural wins with tests before the run, so a regression fails loudly.

**4. AC9 → AC10** — the live re-test, both score layers, then the honest report.

# ⚑ AMENDMENT 1 — Larry, 2026-08-12, after Keel's CLARIFY read-back

**All thirteen findings resolved below. This amendment is OPERATIVE and supersedes anything above it that
it contradicts.** Per `CLAUDE.md`, this earns ONE further read-back; after that, proceed.

## The finding that changes the experiment — F1 UPHELD, AC5's geometry is REDEFINED

**Keel established by execution that the photograph is rotated ~90° and written in two columns.**
Ink-density profiling of the paper box found **~21 alternating ink bands along the X axis and none along
Y**; EXIF orientation reads `null`, so nothing ever corrected for it. **The handwritten lines stack along
X and run along Y.**

**Every horizontal strip ever cut has sliced every line perpendicular. No strip has ever contained a whole
line — only the full-page region has.** That is almost certainly why the model requested region 1 mid-loop
in both WP-B15-29 arms: it was reaching for the only region in which the writing was legible.

**Consequence: AC5 as written would have made the result WORSE**, cutting each line into 6–8 fragments.
Overlap does not rescue it, because the failure is not lines falling near a seam — it is no line being
whole in any band.

**AUTHORISED, and this is Larry's ruling within Warwick's stated intent** (*"smaller deterministic
application-owned regions/bands... give Terra enough visual resolution per handwritten line"*): build the
finer plan **in-surface** and make it **orientation-aware**. Determine the text-stacking axis
**deterministically from the ink profile — application-owned, model-free; Terra never proposes
coordinates** — then cut 6–8 bands **perpendicular to the reading direction**, retaining modest overlap.
The band COUNT and the overlap are Warwick's; the AXIS was wrong in the order and is corrected here.
**Handle the two columns explicitly**: report whether you band per column or across both, and why.

## F2 UPHELD — the coverage proof was vacuous. Use Keel's form.

*"Every line falls inside at least one region"* is trivially true forever, because region 1 covers the
page. **Replaced by:** for every position on the stacking axis, a band of one line-height centred there is
**fully contained, with margin, inside at least one NON-full-page region**. That is what *"no line sits
only at a boundary"* actually means, it is checkable by geometry, and it **fails on the current plan** — a
decision-grade fact available before any spend. Report the old plan's failure and the new plan's pass.

## F8 UPHELD — resolution is likely the binding constraint. Upscaling AUTHORISED, as its own arm.

~22 px per handwritten line, and `renderRegionCrop()` is a pure `extract` with **no resize** — so every
crop to date has handed the model *exactly the same pixels*, reducing competing content without adding one
bit of information. **Authorised: deterministic, application-owned upscaling of each band** (e.g. 3×
lanczos).

**Run TWO arms so the gain is attributable, because this moves two variables:**
- **Arm C — orientation-aware bands, NO upscale.**
- **Arm D — orientation-aware bands, WITH upscale.**

Warwick on cost, quoted: *"If better region coverage doubles or even modestly exceeds that cost but
produces a trustworthy weekly shop, that is economically sane... **Do not save pennies by accepting
rubbish.**"* **If Arm C already clears the bar, Arm D is optional — say so rather than spending for
symmetry.**
